reviewer.actual_effort: Low-to-moderate. I read all six split images (s96 parts 1–3, s97 parts 1–3) and the full s96.jpg once for context. I compared the dossier units yishtabbach through or_olam against the print, and read the human decisions file. I did not open the independent blind-response JSONs (no glob tool), did not re-read the full s97.jpg, and did not do a mark-by-mark magnified check of every vowel, dagesh, meteg or accent.

citation_and_instruction_findings.finding: The Hebrew-page instruction is printed as 'The Reader says half Kaddish.', which matches the current he-witness instruction. It is printed before וְעַתָּה. No change needed.
The speaker labels are printed as פֿאָרבעטער: (with rafe on the pe), געמיינדע: and קו״ח (small, above the response). These match the current text.
The running header reads 34 · יוֹצֵר לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה · 34. It is not body text and I made no finding on it.

source_findings.reason: There is no comma after 'Holy One' in the print. This contrasts with the Kaddish paragraph on the same page, which does print 'the Holy One, blessed be He;'.

citation_and_instruction_findings.finding: The English-page instruction is printed as 'The reader recites half Kaddish.' (lowercase 'reader'), which matches the current en-witness instruction.

The print runs both verses together in one English block ('…as Thou hast said: Remember Thy mercy…'). The current text splits them into two units with the same wording. That is acceptable structurally, and there is no text change.

The printed English 'Blessed be Him, His Name is exalted above and ever.' is reproduced faithfully. It is a garbled translation of בשכמל״ו, not a typesetting typo, so I propose no sic/corr. An editorial note is optional.
'eter-nity' is hyphenated only because of the line break. The current 'eternity' is correct.
The Hebrew linkage cues (ישתבח, ועתה, יתגדל, ברכו, אור) were deliberately left out, as instructed. They are not substantive omissions.

coverage_limits: I judged scans 96–97 only. I did not consult the independent blind-response JSONs. The human decisions file has no entries for s96–97, so nothing from it was reopened. I compared vowels, dagesh, meteg and accents at the resolution of the split images and did not magnify them mark by mark. Only the items listed under unresolved are explicitly flagged, but any other fine marks are not certified beyond what I visibly compared. I cannot recommend accepting the s96 source text until the three Kaddish corrections are applied and the unresolved items are settled. I recommend accepting s97 once the one comma correction is applied.
